topics.label: REST Principles
topics.desc: Roy Fielding's architectural style for networked systems built on a uniform interface, client-server separation, statelessness, cacheability, and layering over HTTP.

topics.label: Resources & URIs
topics.desc: Modeling the domain as nouns (resources like /users/42/orders) addressed by stable URIs, the central abstraction REST clients fetch and manipulate representations of.

topics.label: HTTP Method Semantics
topics.desc: Mapping CRUD onto GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE with correct safe and idempotent semantics so caches, proxies, and clients behave predictably.

topics.label: Status Codes
topics.desc: Using standard HTTP response codes (2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error) like 200, 201, 404, and 422 to convey outcomes.

topics.label: Statelessness
topics.desc: The REST constraint that each request carries all context the server needs, holding no client session state, which simplifies horizontal scaling and load balancing.

topics.label: Content Negotiation
topics.desc: Clients and servers agreeing on representation via Accept, Content-Type, and Accept-Language headers to serve JSON, XML, or other media types from one URI.

topics.label: HATEOAS
topics.desc: Hypermedia As The Engine Of Application State: responses embed links (e.g. HAL, JSON:API) so clients discover available actions dynamically rather than hardcoding URLs.

topics.label: Richardson Maturity Model
topics.desc: A four-level scale (0 to 3) grading API RESTfulness by adoption of resources, HTTP verbs, and hypermedia controls, with level 3 being full HATEOAS.

topics.label: Resource Modeling
topics.desc: Designing the API's nouns, relationships, nesting, and naming conventions (plural lowercase nouns, sub-resources, singletons) so the surface maps cleanly to the domain.

topics.label: Versioning Strategies
topics.desc: Evolving an API without breaking clients via URI versions (/v2), header or media-type versioning, and deprecation policies that signal sunset timelines.

topics.label: Pagination
topics.desc: Returning large collections in chunks using offset/limit or cursor-based (keyset) pagination, the latter being more stable and performant for changing datasets.

topics.label: Filtering & Sorting
topics.desc: Letting clients shape collection responses through query parameters for filtering, sorting, field selection (sparse fieldsets), and full-text search criteria.

topics.label: Idempotency
topics.desc: Designing operations so repeated identical requests have one effect, often via client-supplied Idempotency-Key headers that make retries on payments safe.

topics.label: Error Response Design
topics.desc: Returning structured, machine-readable errors with consistent shapes, often the RFC 7807/9457 Problem Details JSON format carrying type, title, and detail fields.

topics.label: Rate Limiting
topics.desc: Throttling clients to protect capacity using token-bucket or fixed-window algorithms, signaling limits via 429 responses and X-RateLimit or Retry-After headers.

topics.label: API Keys & Tokens
topics.desc: Identifying and gating callers with API keys or bearer tokens passed in headers; a lightweight access primitive distinct from the full OAuth/auth domain.

topics.label: Schema, SDL & Types
topics.desc: GraphQL's strongly-typed contract in Schema Definition Language, defining Query/Mutation/Subscription roots plus scalars, objects, enums, interfaces, and unions with nullability.

topics.label: Queries & Mutations
topics.desc: Client-specified read operations whose request shape dictates exact response fields (eliminating over-fetching) and write operations that mutate state and return results in one round trip.

topics.label: Subscriptions
topics.desc: GraphQL's real-time operation type that pushes server events to clients over a persistent transport, typically WebSockets via the graphql-ws protocol.

topics.label: Resolvers
topics.desc: Per-field server functions that fetch each piece of a GraphQL response from databases or services, composing the graph the schema describes.

topics.label: N+1 & DataLoader
topics.desc: The query explosion where naive resolvers issue one DB call per item, solved by DataLoader, which batches and caches lookups within a single request.

topics.label: Apollo & Tooling
topics.desc: The GraphQL ecosystem of servers and clients such as Apollo Server, Apollo Client, urql, Relay, and GraphQL Yoga that handle execution, caching, and codegen.

topics.label: Schema Federation
topics.desc: Composing one supergraph from multiple service subgraphs (Apollo Federation, schema stitching) so teams own slices of a unified GraphQL API independently.

topics.label: GraphQL vs REST
topics.desc: Trade-offs between GraphQL's flexible single-endpoint queries and REST's cacheable resource endpoints, weighing client flexibility against caching and operational simplicity.

topics.label: RPC Model
topics.desc: The Remote Procedure Call paradigm of invoking a function on a remote service as if it were local, framing APIs around actions rather than resources.

topics.label: gRPC
topics.desc: Google's high-performance RPC framework using HTTP/2 transport and Protocol Buffers, popular for low-latency internal microservice communication across many languages.

topics.label: Protocol Buffers
topics.desc: Google's language-neutral binary serialization format defined in .proto schemas, compiled into typed client and server stubs and powering gRPC's compact wire encoding.

topics.label: Streaming RPC
topics.desc: gRPC's server-streaming, client-streaming, and bidirectional-streaming call modes over a single HTTP/2 connection, enabling efficient long-lived data flows.

topics.label: tRPC
topics.desc: A TypeScript framework giving end-to-end type-safe APIs without codegen or schemas, inferring client types directly from server router definitions in monorepos.

topics.label: JSON-RPC
topics.desc: A minimal, transport-agnostic RPC protocol encoding method calls as JSON objects, used in blockchain nodes, the Language Server Protocol, and lightweight services.

topics.label: WebSockets
topics.desc: A full-duplex, persistent TCP connection upgraded from HTTP that lets server and client push messages freely, underpinning chat, live dashboards, and games.

topics.label: Server-Sent Events
topics.desc: A unidirectional stream of server-to-client events over a long-lived HTTP response via the EventSource API, with built-in auto-reconnect and simpler than WebSockets.

topics.label: Long Polling
topics.desc: A near-real-time fallback where the client holds an HTTP request open until the server has data, then immediately reconnects, used before WebSocket support.

topics.label: Socket.IO
topics.desc: A JavaScript library layering rooms, automatic reconnection, and transport fallback over WebSockets, simplifying robust bidirectional messaging for Node apps.

topics.label: WebRTC
topics.desc: A browser standard for peer-to-peer audio, video, and data channels using ICE/STUN/TURN for NAT traversal, powering video calls without routing media through servers.

topics.label: Pub/Sub Patterns
topics.desc: The publish-subscribe model decoupling senders from receivers via channels or topics, used to fan out real-time events through Redis, NATS, or managed services.

topics.label: Presence & Broadcasting
topics.desc: Tracking which users are online and broadcasting state to a channel, a common real-time feature offered by platforms like Pusher, Ably, and Phoenix Channels.

topics.label: OpenAPI & Swagger
topics.desc: The dominant standard for describing REST APIs in a machine-readable YAML/JSON spec, rendered as interactive docs by Swagger UI and consumed by countless tools.

topics.label: Contract-First Design
topics.desc: Authoring the API spec before implementation as the single source of truth, letting frontend and backend teams build in parallel against an agreed interface.

topics.label: API Mocking
topics.desc: Generating fake servers from a spec (Prism, Mockoon, MSW) so clients develop and test against realistic responses before the real backend exists.

topics.label: SDK Generation
topics.desc: Auto-producing typed client libraries and server stubs from an OpenAPI or gRPC spec using tools like openapi-generator, Swagger Codegen, or Speakeasy.

topics.label: Postman & Insomnia
topics.desc: Interactive GUI tools for exploring, testing, and documenting APIs through saved request collections, environments, and automated test suites.

topics.label: Contract Testing
topics.desc: Verifying that a provider's responses match what consumers expect, often consumer-driven with Pact, catching breaking changes before they reach production.

topics.label: API Blueprint & RAML
topics.desc: Alternative Markdown- and YAML-based API description languages that predate or compete with OpenAPI for documenting and designing HTTP interfaces.

topics.label: HTTP Clients
topics.desc: Libraries for calling APIs from code, such as the browser/Node fetch API, axios, and ky, handling requests, headers, bodies, and response parsing.

topics.label: Webhooks
topics.desc: Reverse APIs where a provider POSTs event notifications to your registered URL, used by Stripe and GitHub, requiring signature verification and idempotent handling.

topics.label: Third-Party Integration
topics.desc: Consuming external services like Stripe, Twilio, or the Google APIs by reading docs, managing credentials, mapping their data models, and handling their quirks.

topics.label: OAuth Client Flows
topics.desc: From the consumer side, obtaining access tokens to call protected third-party APIs via authorization-code or client-credentials grants; full auth lives in its own domain.

topics.label: Retries & Backoff
topics.desc: Making integrations resilient to transient failures with exponential backoff, jitter, timeouts, and circuit breakers so retries do not amplify outages.

topics.label: API Gateways
topics.desc: A single entry point fronting backend services to handle routing, auth, rate limiting, and aggregation, via products like Kong, AWS API Gateway, and Apigee.

topics.label: CORS for APIs
topics.desc: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers that let an API authorize browser requests from other origins, including preflight OPTIONS handling for non-simple requests.
